character.centerRule: David son of Jesse remains the stable human center; Chronicles parallels, royal evaluations, poems, prophetic images, genealogies, titles, quotations, and Jesus-related Davidic language remain attached to their own inspectable canonical sources.

phases.orientation: A Bethlehem genealogy reaches David; Samuel selects the youngest son, the spirit comes on him, and music brings him into Saul’s court.
phases.title: Ancestry, Anointing, and Court

phases.orientation: David enters the Philistine challenge, becomes bound to Jonathan and Saul’s household, and meets affection, praise, marriage, jealousy, and open pursuit.
phases.title: Battle, Fame, and Saul’s House

phases.orientation: Weapons, bread, refuge, endangered communities, Jonathan’s covenant, Saul’s pursuit, Abigail’s interruption, and two spared lives shape David before the throne.
phases.title: Flight, Covenant, and Restraint

phases.orientation: David shelters with Achish, approaches a battle against Israel, is dismissed by Philistine rulers, returns to loss at Ziklag, and learns of Saul’s death.
phases.title: Philistine Brink and Recovery

phases.orientation: Lament, inquiry, partial kingship, civil conflict, rejected shortcuts, all-Israel recognition, Jerusalem, family growth, and Philistine battles gather around the new king.
phases.title: Judah, Conflict, and Unification

phases.orientation: The ark’s movement, fear, celebration, household tension, David’s building desire, God’s house promise, prayer, warfare, administration, covenant kindness, and international conflict fill the settled reign.
phases.title: Ark, House, and Kingdom

phases.orientation: David sends and takes, Nathan tells and accuses, consequences enter the household, a child dies, Solomon is born, Tamar is violated, Amnon dies, and Absalom returns without repair.
phases.title: Taking, Rebuke, and House Fracture

phases.orientation: Absalom’s conspiracy drives David from Jerusalem; loyalty, humiliation, counsel, battle, grief, contested return, and another rebellion expose a kingdom still divided.
phases.title: Exile, Return, and Rebellion

phases.orientation: Inherited violence, Rizpah’s vigil, warrior limits, deliverance poetry, last words, named companions, census guilt, plague, intercession, altar, and purchased ground close Samuel’s account.
phases.title: Famine, Song, Last Words, and Census

phases.orientation: Solomon’s succession and David’s death stand beside Chronicles’ expanded memory of Jerusalem, warriors, ark, worship, promise, census, Temple preparation, public assembly, and final prayer.
phases.title: Succession, Retelling, and Temple Preparation

phases.orientation: Kings are measured through David, poems and prayers carry his name and promise, prophets reuse throne, shepherd, branch, tent, and covenant language, and later Jewish writings remember his life.
phases.title: Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory

phases.orientation: Genealogies, healings, entry cries, debates, speeches, letters, and Revelation invoke David, his throne, his psalms, his key, his root, and his descendant in distinct arguments.
phases.title: Gospel and Apostolic Memory

character.throughline: David moves from Bethlehem shepherd and Saul’s servant through public victory, covenant friendship, pursuit, restraint, Philistine refuge, partial and united kingship, Jerusalem, ark and house promise, royal taking, household fracture, exile, return, census, succession, Temple preparation, and wide later memory.

points.right: Elders of every tribe name kinship and prior leadership.

points.right: The elders arrive after Saul’s house and David’s partial kingship.

nodes.title: Israel later seeks the LORD and David their king

nodes.note: The fallen tent is repaired, nations are possessed, harvest overtakes harvest, cities are rebuilt, vineyards and gardens are planted, and the people are planted in their land.
nodes.title: David’s fallen tent is raised amid restored land

pivots.title: Follow branch, shepherd, tent, and covenant

pivots.description: Move from Ruth’s Bethlehem line through Matthew and Luke’s different structures.

nodes.note: Ruth’s closing movement joins birth, neighborhood naming, Obed, Jesse, and David in one family line.
nodes.title: A Bethlehem genealogy reaches David

nodes.note: The genealogy opens with Jesus Christ as son of David and Abraham, moves through David the king and Uriah’s wife, exile, and fourteen-generation divisions.
nodes.title: David becomes a hinge in Matthew’s genealogy

nodes.note: The genealogy moves backward from Jesus through Joseph and Heli, reaches Nathan and David, then continues through Abraham and Adam to God.
nodes.title: Luke’s genealogy passes through Nathan and David

pivots.title: Follow David in genealogies

pivots.description: Trace mercy cries, public acclaim, lineage answers, and Jesus’ question about David’s Lord.

nodes.note: The men follow Jesus crying for mercy, answer his question about belief, receive touch and sight, and spread the report despite a warning.
nodes.title: Two blind men call Jesus Son of David

nodes.note: The woman cries for mercy and her daughter, meets silence and disciple pressure, debates lost sheep and household crumbs, is commended for faith, and her daughter is healed.
nodes.title: A Canaanite woman calls the Son of David

nodes.note: The crowd tries to silence two men who call Jesus Lord and Son of David; Jesus stops, asks their desire, touches their eyes, and they follow.
nodes.title: Two blind men call from the Jericho road

nodes.note: A blind beggar hears Jesus is passing, cries “Son of David,” persists through rebuke, throws off his cloak, names his request, receives sight, and follows on the way.
nodes.title: Bartimaeus calls Jesus Son of David

nodes.note: Jesus rides into Jerusalem, crowds use royal psalm language, the city asks who he is, Temple commerce is overturned, blind and lame people are healed, and children cry “Hosanna to the son of David.”
nodes.title: Son of David cries enter Jerusalem and the Temple

nodes.note: Pharisees answer that the Christ is David’s son; Jesus cites David speaking by the Spirit in Psalm 110 and asks how the son is also called Lord.
nodes.title: Jesus asks how the Christ is David’s son and Lord

pivots.title: Follow “Son of David”

pivots.description: Trace the deliverance song, its Psalter witness, David’s last-word frame, Jesus’ Temple question, and Peter’s Pentecost argument.

nodes.note: David sings of rock, distress, cosmic response, rescue, paths, combat, peoples, and steadfast love to the king and his offspring.
nodes.title: David interprets deliverance in a long song

nodes.note: The psalm moves through love, refuge, distress, cosmic descent, rescue, paths, conflict, peoples, and steadfast love to the king and offspring.
nodes.title: Deliverance is sung again as a psalm

nodes.note: David identifies himself through ancestry, anointing, song, and divine speech; just rule is compared to morning light and an everlasting covenant is named beside worthless thorns.
nodes.title: Last words join spirit, rule, and covenant

nodes.note: Pharisees answer that the Christ is David’s son; Jesus cites David speaking by the Spirit in Psalm 110 and asks how the son is also called Lord.
nodes.title: Jesus asks how the Christ is David’s son and Lord

nodes.note: Peter speaks of Jesus’ death and resurrection, quotes David from Psalm 16, distinguishes David’s tomb, recalls the oath about his throne, and cites Psalm 110 before naming Jesus Lord and Christ.
nodes.title: Peter reads David’s psalm through resurrection and throne

pivots.title: Follow Davidic psalm speech

pivots.description: Trace psalms, throne oath, fallen tent, descent, forgiveness, rest, witness catalogue, key, root, and offspring.

nodes.note: Peter speaks of Jesus’ death and resurrection, quotes David from Psalm 16, distinguishes David’s tomb, recalls the oath about his throne, and cites Psalm 110 before naming Jesus Lord and Christ.
nodes.title: Peter reads David’s psalm through resurrection and throne

nodes.note: Released apostles report threats; the community names God as creator, says the Holy Spirit spoke through David in Psalm 2, identifies gathered rulers around Jesus, and asks for bold speech.
nodes.title: The gathered believers pray David’s words about rulers

nodes.note: Paul recounts Israel from Egypt through judges and Saul, says God raised David and testified about his heart and will, then announces Jesus from David’s offspring.
nodes.title: Paul moves from David’s selection to a Savior from his offspring

nodes.note: James responds to the Gentile report, says prophetic words agree, quotes the restored tent of David and nations called by God’s name, and proposes a limited written judgment.
nodes.title: James cites the rebuilding of David’s fallen tent

nodes.note: Paul introduces himself, the gospel promised through prophets, Jesus descended from David according to flesh, declared Son of God in power by resurrection, and a calling among nations.
nodes.title: Paul names Jesus as David’s descendant and God’s Son

nodes.note: Paul asks about Abraham, contrasts work and trust, then says David pronounces blessing on the person credited righteousness apart from works and quotes forgiven lawlessness and covered sins.
nodes.title: David speaks of forgiveness in Paul’s Abraham argument

nodes.note: The argument holds promise of entering rest, creation’s seventh day, wilderness unbelief, Joshua, and a later day designated through David’s “Today,” then urges diligence.
nodes.title: A later “Today” is located in David

nodes.note: A sealed scroll prompts weeping until an elder announces the Lion of Judah and Root of David has overcome; the seer then sees a slain-standing Lamb who takes the scroll and receives a new song.
nodes.title: The Root of David is announced before a Lamb appears

nodes.note: The coming speaker names beginning and end, blessing and exclusion surround the city, Jesus says he is David’s root and offspring and the bright morning star, and Spirit, bride, and hearers say “Come.”
nodes.title: Jesus names himself David’s root and offspring

pivots.title: Follow David in apostolic argument

pivots.description: Hold Sirach’s praise, Maccabean exhortation, Kings’ evaluation, and Samuel’s difficult close together.

nodes.note: David is placed after Nathan, compared to fat separated from an offering, remembered for beasts and Goliath, praised for songs, and credited with arranging festival worship.
nodes.title: Sirach remembers lion, bear, Goliath, praise, and worship

nodes.note: The portrait says the Lord took away David’s sins, exalted his power, gave a covenant and throne, then moves through Solomon’s wisdom, desire, and the kingdom’s division.
nodes.title: Sirach retains pardon, covenant, and the division after David

nodes.note: Mattathias calls his sons to zeal and fidelity, names ancestors as examples, says David inherited a royal throne because he was merciful, assigns leadership, and dies.
nodes.title: A deathbed exhortation remembers David’s mercy

nodes.note: Abijam’s sins and heart are contrasted with David, while a lamp in Jerusalem is preserved for David’s sake and Uriah is named as David’s exception.
nodes.title: Abijam is measured against David’s heart

nodes.note: Gad directs an altar; Araunah offers place, animals, and wood, but David insists on purchase, pays fifty silver shekels for floor and oxen, sacrifices, and the plague is stopped.
nodes.title: David buys the threshing floor and builds an altar

pivots.title: Follow later portraits of David
